children: shares fell nearly 5% Monday as investors considered whether the memory-chip maker could eventually pursue a stock split after its share price reached four-digit territory.

Sandisk closed at $1,551.99, while its 52-week range stretches from $89.56 to $2,354.39. The company has about 146 million shares outstanding, helping explain why its per-share price is much higher than many companies with similar market values.

A split would change the number of shares held by investors but would not alter Sandisk's underlying business or market capitalization. The company generated $20.25 billion in fiscal 2026 revenue, up 175% from a year earlier, while net income reached $11.4 billion.
Sandisk also has a $15.5 billion repurchase authorization after adding $14 billion in August. Buybacks can reduce shares outstanding, moving in the opposite direction from a stock split.

A split could have greater relevance for the Dow Jones Industrial Average, which uses share prices to determine member weights. Sandisk's current price could make inclusion more difficult without a split, although such a move would not guarantee entry.

title: Sandisk $1,500 Stock Price Ignites Fresh Split Frenzy
